title: Stochastic sampling & lossy-channel metering reconciliation for streaming requests
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: We've observed rare but reproducible billing spikes for streaming requests that use nondeterministic sampling (top-p / nucleus) and speculative decoding. Root cause hypothesis: when intermittent transport loss (WebSocket frame drops, proxy retries) causes clients or edge proxies to replay or patch missing fragments, the server-side metering pipeline sometimes records duplicate output tokens. Duplicate credits occur because sampling randomness produces different final tokens for re-sent prompt prefixes and the ledger lacks a collision-resistant idempotency key tied to the stochastic decision path. This ticket designs and implements a lightweight de-duplication and reconciliation protocol that is backward compatible and minimizes runtime overhead.
acceptance_criteria: Metering ledger deduplicates duplicate output fragments caused by replayed streaming fragments at 99.999% effectiveness in simulated packet-loss tests
No measurable latency regression (>1%) for steady-state streaming at p50/p95 after opt-in flag enabled
Retroactive correction job can detect and fix duplicate credits for a 7-day window and produce a reconciliation report
New telemetry surfaces sampling-mode spikes (top-p, temp) and maps excessive delta-credits per request to a trace ID
progress_updates: 2026-03-10 - Triage: reported after incident CS-2026-03-08 where a customer saw a 4x quota burn on a 12-hour streaming job. Initial hypothesis recorded and engineering triage assigned.

2026-03-11 - Spike repro harness: QA created a deterministic harness that injects packet drops and varying sampling seeds; reproduced duplicate-credit pattern on staging (see run: https://ci.redwood-inference.internal/builds/1257).

2026-03-12 - Design review: proposed solution of (1) fragment-level entropy-hash (entropy-hash = H(prefix_bytes || sampler-seed || generation-offset)) stored with fragment ledger, (2) sequence+entropy idempotency check on finalization, (3) reconciliation job to dedupe historical duplicates. Design doc posted to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/METER/Stochastic+Sampling+Reconciliation

2026-03-13 - Prototype: implemented entropy-hash computation and in-memory dedupe check behind feature flag stream.dedupe_entropy. Microbenchmark shows 0.4% p50 latency overhead in local GPU runtime. PR created: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/pull/8621
technical_design: High level: add a 64-bit entropy-hash to every streaming fragment at the point where sampling is performed. The hash uses a fast non-cryptographic mixing function (xxhash64) over (prefix_bytes, 64-bit sampler-seed, relative-token-offset, model-variant-id). Ledger entries include fragment_seq and entropy_hash. On fragment finalization we perform an idempotency lookup by (session_id, fragment_seq, entropy_hash). If an entry already exists, the fragment is marked 'duplicate' and no credits are emitted. Compatibility: when feature flag is off, behavior is unchanged. Reconciliation: a daily batch job scans the ledger for near-duplicate fragments (same session_id and overlapping offsets) and applies credit reversals with audit entries. We also add a webhooks/audit CSV output for customers affected by retro-crediting. Edge cases: attachments/pre-tokenized inputs include client-declared token length; we canonicalize using server tokenizer before hashing to avoid client-side mismatch. We intentionally avoid changing token counting logic; dedupe only prevents double-debits on output fragments.
testing_plan: Unit tests: entropy-hash invariants, collision rates below 1e-12 against random seeds
Property tests: fuzz sampler-seed + prefix permutations to ensure no false positives for non-replayed fragments
Integration: staging harness with configurable packet loss and proxy retry patterns (0%, 0.1%, 1%, 5% loss) and multiple sampling modes (greedy, top-k, top-p, temp=1.0)
Load test: 50k concurrent streaming sessions on staging with dedupe flag on to quantify overhead and memory growth
Reconciliation dry-run: run backfill logic in dry-run mode for a 7-day window and compare suspected duplicates with manual audit
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout: enable stream.dedupe_entropy=false by default
Canary: enable for 1% of traffic (internal tenants) for 48 hours, observe delta-credit rates and latencies
Heat up: escalate to 10% for 72 hours if no regressions, then 50% for 48 hours
Full enable: 100% enable after 7-day observation and successful reconciliation dry-run
Backfill: run reconciliation job targeting affected timeframe; process in batches with throttling to avoid DB load
Customer notification: publish audit CSV to S3 and notify customers with potential retro credits via support channel
monitoring_queries: Query: sum(meter.delta_credits) by sampling_mode over 1h to detect top-p anomalies
Alert: increase >10x in delta_credits for sampling_mode=top-p and stream_enabled=true triggers PagerDuty
Dashboard: per-model heatmap of duplicate_fragment_rate and per-region ledger write latency
reviewer_feedback: 2026-03-12 - PM (Jordan Lee): support retro-crediting but prefer opt-in early to limit customer surprise. Agreed to include customer-facing audit CSV and SLA note.
2026-03-13 - Infra (María Gutierrez): suggested swapping xxhash64 for SipHash when ledger entries traverse untrusted proxies; decided to keep xxhash64 but add HMAC if proxy-exposed in future release.
2026-03-13 - Security (Dev): confirmed no secret material in entropy-hash; recommended logging only hash (no seeds) and mark seed telemetry as redacted
